This integration makes **Environment and Climate Change Canada** the weather
provider of Gladys. The dashboard weather widget and the assistant ("what
will the weather be like tomorrow?") use its official forecasts. It adds what
you need in Canada: the official alerts, the **Air Quality Health Index**
(wildfire smoke included), the humidex in summer, the wind chill in winter
and the precipitation radar.

Nothing to enter, no account, no key: everything comes from the open services
of the Meteorological Service of Canada, for the location of your house.
**Canada only.**

## Installation

1. Install the integration from the Gladys catalog (Gladys 5.1 or newer).
2. Accept the access to the **location of your houses**: the weather is the
   one of the house, nothing else to enter.
3. Check that your house is placed on the map (**Settings → Houses**).
   Without a location, there is no weather.
4. In the **Configuration** screen, click **Test Environment Canada**: the
   message says what each source answered (forecasts, alerts, air quality).

Once installed, the integration takes precedence over the OpenWeather service
built into Gladys. The weather widget can also pick it explicitly.

## Where the weather comes from

The forecasts are those of the Environment Canada **city page** nearest to
your house (the same as on weather.gc.ca): current conditions measured at the
station of the city, 24 hours of hourly forecasts and about 6 days. The
"Feels like" widget names the city used.

## Configuration

- **Official alerts** (on by default) — Environment Canada warnings,
  watches, advisories and statements covering your house, special air
  quality and smoke statements included. They show in the weather widget and
  feed the "Weather alert" scene trigger of Gladys. When an alert appears,
  changes level or ends, the integration tells Gladys within minutes instead
  of waiting for its 30-minute check.
- **Air quality alerts** (off by default) — adds an alert when the Air
  Quality Health Index of your area reaches a high risk (7 or more). Not an
  official alert: it comes from the index itself.
- **Feels-like alerts (estimates)** (off by default) — adds an alert when
  the computed humidex or wind chill reaches a real risk (great discomfort,
  high risk of frostbite…). They are not official alerts.
- **Precipitation radar** (on by default) — a 300 × 200 km radar image
  centered on your house. Turn on the "provider images" option of the
  weather widget to see it.

## The "Air quality" widget

The **Air Quality Health Index** (AQHI) of Health Canada and Environment
Canada runs from 1 to 10+. It combines ozone, fine particles and nitrogen
dioxide. The widget shows:

- the index **now** and its **risk level**, on a gauge;
- the **peak of the next 24 hours** and the hour-by-hour forecast;
- the forecast by period (tonight, tomorrow…);
- in wildfire season, the index expected **in the smoke**, when Environment
  Canada publishes one;
- the **official advice**, for everyone and for the people at risk (heart or
  lung conditions, children, older adults).

The index is the one of the nearest **community** (about 130 in Canada),
75 km away at most. Some communities have a forecast but no measurement
(Montréal and Québec City, whose air is measured by the province): the index
of the current hour is then the forecast one, and the widget says so.

| AQHI     | Risk level |
| -------- | ---------- |
| 1 to 3   | Low        |
| 4 to 6   | Moderate   |
| 7 to 10  | High       |
| Above 10 | Very high  |

**House** setting: the name of the house to show. Empty, it is the first
located house.

## The "Feels like" widget

It shows:

- the index that applies now: **humidex** from 20 °C, else **wind chill**,
  with its **risk level** on the Environment Canada scales;
- the temperature and, in winter, the wind chill **in the gusts** (in
  summer, the dew point);
- the feels-like and the temperature of the next 24 hours, with the **worst
  hour**;
- the **time to frostbite** of exposed skin, the **muggy night** (night dew
  point of 18 °C or more), the **black ice risk** (freezing rain, freezing
  fog or precipitation around 0 °C) and the 3-hour **pressure trend**.

### The feels-like levels

| Level                | Index                                             |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- |
| Extreme cold risk    | wind chill of −55 or less (frostbite under 2 min) |
| Severe cold risk     | −48 to −54 (frostbite in 2 to 5 min)              |
| Very high cold risk  | −40 to −47 (frostbite in 5 to 10 min)             |
| High cold risk       | −28 to −39 (frostbite in 10 to 30 min)            |
| Moderate cold risk   | −10 to −27                                        |
| Low risk             | the rest                                          |
| Some discomfort      | humidex 30 to 39                                  |
| Great discomfort     | humidex 40 to 45                                  |
| Dangerous heat       | humidex 46 to 53                                  |
| Heat stroke imminent | humidex 54 or more                                |

## Scenes

Two triggers, checked every 5 minutes:

- **Air quality level changed** — the Air Quality Health Index of a house
  reaches a new risk level.
- **Feels-like level changed** — the humidex or the wind chill of a house
  reaches a new level.

Filters, all optional:

- **Level reached** — e.g. "High risk". The scene fires even when the index
  jumps over this level (from "low" to "very high").
- **Direction** — "Getting worse" or "Getting better".
- **House** — the exact name of the house in Gladys (empty = all).

The next actions can read `{{triggerEvent.data.summary}}` (a sentence ready
to send), `{{triggerEvent.data.value}}`,
`{{triggerEvent.data.current_level}}`, etc.

Examples: close the windows and turn off the air exchanger when the air
quality reaches "High risk" (wildfire smoke); close the blinds and start the
air conditioning at "Great discomfort"; turn on the block heater or send a
notification at "High cold risk".

To avoid bursts, a level is only left with a margin of one unit, and the
first evaluation after a start fires nothing.

## Good to know

- **Outside Canada**: Environment Canada has no weather for your house; the
  integration says so in the Configuration screen.
- The Environment Canada hourly forecasts give no precipitation amount, only
  a probability.
- When Environment Canada does not answer, the last known weather stays shown
  for up to 3 hours.
- The data is cached 10 minutes (5 for the alerts, 15 for the air quality).

## Sources and licences

Data: Environment and Climate Change Canada (city page forecasts, alerts, Air
Quality Health Index, radar), under the ECCC Data Servers End-use Licence.
Radar base map: Natural Resources Canada, under the Open Government Licence –
Canada. The AQHI advice is Health Canada's, sometimes shortened. This
integration is neither affiliated with nor endorsed by the Government of
Canada.

## Parámetros de configuración

Estos son los parámetros que Environment Canada te pide en su pantalla de configuración en Gladys.

| Parámetro | Tipo | Obligatorio | Descripción |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Environment Canada weather | `section` | No | The official forecasts of Environment and Climate Change Canada for the location of your house in Gladys: nothing to enter, no account, no key. Canada only. The data come from the open Meteorological Service of Canada services (Open Government Licence – Canada); this integration is not affiliated with the Government of Canada. |
| Official alerts | `boolean` | No | Warnings, watches, advisories and statements of Environment Canada for your house, air quality and wildfire smoke statements included. They feed the weather widget and the core “weather alert” scene trigger. |
| Air quality alerts (AQHI) | `boolean` | No | Adds an alert when the Air Quality Health Index of your area reaches a high risk (7 or more). Not an official alert: it comes from the index itself. |
| Feels-like alerts (estimates) | `boolean` | No | Adds an alert when the humidex or the wind chill computed by the integration reaches a real risk. Not official: they mix with the Environment Canada alerts. |
| Precipitation radar | `boolean` | No | Environment Canada radar around your house, shown in the weather widget when its “provider images” option is on. |

## Cómo instalar Environment Canada en Gladys

1. En Gladys, abre **Integraciones**: Environment Canada aparece en el catálogo junto a las integraciones nativas, con una insignia de comunidad.
2. Haz clic en **Instalar**. Gladys descarga la imagen Docker (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-environment-canada:0.1.0`), la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo y genera la interfaz de la integración (dispositivos, descubrimiento y configuración).
3. Abre la pantalla de **Configuración** de la integración, rellena los parámetros y guarda.
4. También puedes instalarla directamente desde la URL de su repositorio: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-environment-canada](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-environment-canada).

Environment Canada requiere Gladys `>=5.1.0`. El catálogo de Gladys se actualiza cada hora, así que una nueva versión está disponible como máximo una hora después de publicarse.

¿Todavía no usas Gladys? Es gratuito y de código abierto: [sigue la guía de instalación](/es/docs/) para empezar.

## Sobre las integraciones externas

Environment Canada es una **integración externa**: una integración comunitaria empaquetada como contenedor Docker y publicada en GitHub. Gladys la instala con un clic y la ejecuta en un entorno aislado del núcleo. La publica y mantiene [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7), no el equipo principal de Gladys.
